title: Alto saxophone
reference_instrument: University of Iowa MIS alto saxophone (maker and model unstated on the page)
summary: Stand-in saxophone, not a measured one. No tone holes: each note is the printed mouthpiece, neck and bell cones joined by one straight cone cut to that note's length, where a real saxophone plays these notes with holes. The reed's opening, width and area are borrowed. C4 is blown at mf, E3 and F3 at ff, because they were silent at mf on this reed before the closure stop (not tried again since). One mouthpiece position, pushed in 13.27 mm and solved once on C4's passive peak on the bore air below, leaves the three, with the reed lay and tongue contact rows below, at +30.8, -6.1 and -3.6 c from equal temperament (+25.6, -8.6 and -6.3 c without the two rows; +26.4, -10.6 and -7.7 c on the pages before them); the passive peaks, solved without the two rows, agree to 0.3 c, so the spread is the reed's pull. All three are cleaner than the recordings, and C4's seventh harmonic sits 8 dB under its sixth. All three pages are re-renders after the reed's closure stop (a857c6f17); on the old law the reed passed through its lay on 17 to 19 % of steady samples. The duct carries a continuous gas field, Noreland 2013's measured bore-air profile of a clarinet (304.15 K at the mouthpiece to 294.96 K at the end of the clarinet's bore, exhaled breath, saturated), borrowed, with its positions scaled to the saxophone's bore by this model's choice; the body's slope and length, the three cuts and the push were re-solved on that air against equal temperament (2026-11-07) and the three pages rendered again. They score 10 of 15, 6 of 14 and 6 of 14 inside the ruler, against 10, 5 and 6: C4 and F3 tie, and E3 rises by one measure, harmonics-to-noise, as its lock falls from 1.000 to 0.978; F3's pitch moves 1.4 c toward equal temperament and away from the recording. The three pages then gained a reed lay profile and a tongue contact row (2026-11-07), every number borrowed from the clarinet cards except Hofmann 2012's printed 34.5 ms alto tonguing contact time: they tie the count again (10 of 15, 6 of 14 and 6 of 14; strict 10, 5 and 5), move the pitch +5.2, +2.5 and +2.7 c, and take no measure across a ruler; C4's pitch and attack gaps to the recording grow, F3's partial trajectory and pitch gaps grow, and E3's three small ones grow (cepstral envelope, partial frequency, harmonics-to-noise). The binary is newer than the previous pages' by two source commits, 276e44fac and 3c332d358; on the previous cards it renders the posted clips byte for byte, so they move 0 samples of them. Ab4 and E5 stay empty: with a register hole borrowed from a soprano they play an octave low. On 2026-11-08 the three pages were rendered again with the reed channel's flow law changed (the separated-jet law of van Zon et al. 1990 in place of the fully developed one, at the cards' own `slit_length 0.025`, the clarinet cards' lay length, borrowed): C4 10 to 10 of 15, E3 6 to 6 of 14, F3 6 to 7 of 14 inside the ruler; the pitch moves +0.5, -0.1 and -0.2 c and the level by -0.8, -0.7 and -0.6 dB. The clarinet mouthpiece's printed channel length, 1.4 mm (Chatziioannou and van Walstijn 2008), was tried on these pages and not used: C4 and F3 were refused at the law's step at L/h = 3 and E3 fell from 6 to 2 of 14. The receiver's grid latency (a quarter of its grid: 2048 samples, 42.7 ms, on C4; 4096 samples, 85.3 ms, on E3 and F3) was removed from the start of every clip on 2026-11-08 with `--compensate-outlet-latency`: each new clip is the previous version's render shifted by those samples, equal to the last bit, so there is no new physics, only the timing; on E3 and F3 the release tail the old clip cut off is now heard (rms 12.5 and 10.0 LSB over the last 4096 samples). The loose count moves from 10 to 9 of 15 on C4 (C4 fall), and stays 6 of 14 on E3 and 7 of 14 on F3 (strict 5 to 4 on E3), because the grader cuts from the detected onset to the end of the clip and removing the latency moves that onset earlier by the same time, so the cut is that much longer; the partial-trajectory measure is the one that crosses its ruler on C4 and E3.
physics_present: The printed neck (ISMA 2007), bell and mouthpiece (Lefebvre 2010) joined by one straight body cone whose slope is set once from the lowest note, Db3, and cut to each note's length, on the bore air below (slope 0.031732, a full body of 0.798097 m)
An alto reed fitted to a Lefebvre mouthpiece (Lefebvre's printed mass per area, resonance and damping); its opening 1.7 mm, width 10 mm and area 7.5e-5 m2 are borrowed
One mouthpiece position for every note, pushed in 13.27 mm, solved once on C4's passive first peak against equal temperament on the bore air below
Fuks and Sundberg 1996 blowing pressures for two alto players
Reed noise, the duct-constriction law (Oldham and Ukpoho 1990), extrapolated, with no level set against a recording
A flanged bell radiating into room air with ISO 9613 absorption, 0.5 m on axis, at 48 kHz because the engine refuses this bell at 96 kHz
A rigid, inelastic reed closure stop at zero opening (commit a857c6f17)

Bore air along the duct: Noreland 2013's measured temperature profile of a clarinet bore (304.15 K to 294.96 K, borrowed), exhaled breath with saturated water vapour, as a continuous gas field; the positions are scaled to the saxophone's bore by this model's choice (1.0783 m / 0.6552 m); the body slope, the cuts and the push are re-solved on it

A reed lay profile in place of the default slit lay (stiffness 6.1725e6, exponent 2.0, onset 0.16 mm, Hunt-Crossley loss 0.0): the stiffness is Chatziioannou and van Walstijn 2012's printed contact stiffness per area for a clarinet reed times this reed's face area, the other three are the clarinet cards' values; borrowed, no saxophone lay is printed

A tongue contact row on the reed from the blow's start (area 2.6e-5 m2, force 0.2 N, effective area 7.5e-5 m2, released from 0.1845 s over 5 ms): a clarinet's contact area and force (Li 2016, Almeida 2017), with the release start set by Hofmann 2012's printed 34.5 ms alto tonguing contact time

The reed channel's flow law: the separated-jet law of van Zon et al. 1990 (measured on a two-dimensional clarinet mouthpiece; its eq. 7 is inconsistent with its eq. 5, so the Poiseuille part is a construction from its eqs. 1, 5 and 6) at the cards' `slit_length 0.025` m, the clarinet cards' lay length, borrowed; quasisteady, laminar

The receiver's grid latency (a quarter of its grid: 2048 samples, 42.7 ms, on C4; 4096 samples, 85.3 ms, on E3 and F3) was removed from the start of every clip on 2026-11-08 with `--compensate-outlet-latency`: each new clip is the previous version's render shifted by those samples, equal to the last bit, so there is no new physics, only the timing; on E3 and F3 the release tail the old clip cut off is now heard (rms 12.5 and 10.0 LSB over the last 4096 samples). The loose count moves from 10 to 9 of 15 on C4 (C4 fall), and stays 6 of 14 on E3 and 7 of 14 on F3 (strict 5 to 4 on E3), because the grader cuts from the detected onset to the end of the clip and removing the latency moves that onset earlier by the same time, so the cut is that much longer; the partial-trajectory measure is the one that crosses its ruler on C4 and E3.
physics_missing: Tone holes, pads, chimneys, key rise and a fingering chart: no measured alto air column is printed, so no hole lattice is built
A measured alto reed opening, width and area: the opening is an unplayed-tip upper bound, the width a tenor reed's and the area Lefebvre's illustrative value

The right pitch: the three sit +30.8, -6.1 and -3.6 c from equal temperament, a 37 c spread, with the passive peaks (solved without the lay and tongue rows) within 0.3 c of it; the spread is the reed's pull, which differs by note, and why is not shown
The recordings' spectra and noise: harmonics-to-noise reads 1.1 to 3.6 dB above the recordings on all three notes, and C4's centroid is 1203 Hz against 403 Hz
The second register: with a register hole borrowed from a soprano, placed by Scavone's rule, Ab4 and E5 sound an octave low, so they stay empty

A measured saxophone bore-air profile: the field is a clarinet's, its position scaling to the saxophone's bore is this model's choice, and E3's lock falls from 1.000 to 0.978 on this air without a traced cause

A saxophone reed's lay and tongue: no lay profile, tongue contact area or tongue force is printed for a saxophone, so the rows are a clarinet's with one alto number (Hofmann 2012's 34.5 ms contact time); the count does not move with them on any of the three notes, and the render's reed-opening trace was not read to show what the tongue row does

The reed channel's length and law: no saxophone channel length is printed, and 0.025 m is the clarinet cards' lay length. The clarinet mouthpiece's printed channel length, 1.4 mm, puts this reed (openings 0.46 to 1.9 mm) at L/h about 1 to 3, on the law's contracted branch, and the law's step at L/h = 3 (a jump with no blend in the print) stopped the render on C4 and F3 (the massive reed's implicit contact solve did not resolve the momentum balance) and cost E3 four measures. The print's data below L/h = 3 give a constant 0.45 +- 0.05 without a stated range of L/h. Unsteady channel inertia is not modelled.
